study.hypothesis: Unused observer backward passes and row allocations impose measurable training/memory overhead but do not change the mathematical no-row BCE gradient. Removing the entire unused observer package should preserve the inherited forward and intended gradient rule. Floating-point scheduling or backward execution may nevertheless change learned trajectories, so equality of final metrics is a prediction rather than an assumption. This is an implementation and cost hypothesis, not a semantic conflict-resolution or new-architecture claim.
